---
title: "Ollama Embeddings"
guide-section: "Building a Store"
---

[Ollama](https://ollama.com) is an easy way to run open-source models on your own computer. You install a single app, pull the models you want with one command, and Ollama serves them from a local background process. Many people know it for chat models, but Ollama also hosts a good selection of embedding models. Using one of those gives you fully local embeddings: no API key, no per-token costs, and nothing leaving your machine.

raghilda connects to Ollama through `EmbeddingOllama`. Ollama provides an OpenAI-compatible API, so `EmbeddingOllama` is a small variant of `EmbeddingOpenAI` with defaults that match a standard Ollama install. This guide covers setting up Ollama, choosing a model, connecting to Ollama on another machine, and fixing the most common errors.

## Installation

First, download and install Ollama from [ollama.com](https://ollama.com/download). Once it's running, pull an embedding model from the command line:

```bash
ollama pull embeddinggemma-2
```

This downloads [EmbeddingGemma 2](https://ollama.com/library/embeddinggemma-2), the model `EmbeddingOllama` uses by default. It's about 1.3 GB, so the first pull can take a few minutes.

You don't need any additional Python packages. `EmbeddingOllama` uses the `openai` client library, which already comes with raghilda.

## Basic usage

With Ollama running and a model pulled, creating a provider requires no configuration at all. The defaults point to Ollama's standard local address and the `embeddinggemma-2:latest` model:

```{python}
#| eval: false
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingOllama

provider = EmbeddingOllama()
```

To use a different model, pass its name exactly as it appears in `ollama list`:

```{python}
#| eval: false
provider = EmbeddingOllama(model="mxbai-embed-large")
```

Then give the provider to a store with the `embed=` argument:

```{python}
#| eval: false
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingOllama

store = DuckDBStore.create(
    location="my_store.db",
    embed=EmbeddingOllama(),
)
```

When the store is created, raghilda embeds a short probe string to find the model's vector size. This means that if Ollama isn't running or the model hasn't been pulled, you'll find out right away (see [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) below).

## Choosing a model

Ollama's library includes several embedding models. These are some popular ones:

| Model | Dimensions | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `embeddinggemma-2` | 768 | The default. A recent multilingual model from Google that also handles code. The `:270m` tag is a much smaller text-only build |
| `nomic-embed-text` | 768 | Smaller and fast, and very widely used |
| `mxbai-embed-large` | 1024 | Higher quality, at the cost of speed and memory |
| `all-minilm` | 384 | The smallest and fastest option |
| `bge-m3` | 1024 | Multilingual, with strong cross-lingual retrieval |

You can browse the full set on [Ollama's model search page](https://ollama.com/search?c=embedding). To see which models you've already pulled, run `ollama list`.

::: {.callout-note}
A store is tied to the model it was created with, because vectors from different models can't be compared. If you switch models, create a new store and re-ingest your documents.
:::

## Connecting to Ollama on another machine

By default, `EmbeddingOllama` connects to `http://localhost:11434/v1`, which is where Ollama listens on the machine it's installed on. If Ollama runs on a different machine (say, a desktop with a good GPU) or on a different port, set `base_url=` to match:

```{python}
#| eval: false
provider = EmbeddingOllama(base_url="http://192.168.1.10:11434/v1")
```

Make sure the URL ends in `/v1`, since that's the path for Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API. Also note that, by default, Ollama only accepts connections from the machine it's running on. To reach it from another machine, start Ollama with the `OLLAMA_HOST` environment variable set to `0.0.0.0` on the server side (see [Ollama's FAQ](https://docs.ollama.com/faq) for details).

Ollama itself doesn't check API keys, so `EmbeddingOllama` sends a placeholder key unless you provide one. The `api_key=` parameter is only needed if you've put Ollama behind a proxy that requires authentication.

## Reconnecting to a store

When you reconnect to a store, raghilda rebuilds the provider from the configuration it saved at creation time. That configuration includes the model name and the `base_url`:

```{python}
#| eval: false
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore

store = DuckDBStore.connect("my_store.db")
```

You don't need any API keys in your environment for this to work. Ollama does need to be running (at the same `base_url`) whenever you add documents or call `retrieve()`, though, and the model has to still be pulled.

::: {.callout-tip}
Since Ollama's API is OpenAI-compatible, you might wonder why not use `EmbeddingOpenAI` with `base_url` pointing at Ollama. That does work for creating a store, but the store would remember it as an OpenAI provider, and reconnecting would then fail unless `OPENAI_API_KEY` happened to be set. `EmbeddingOllama` is saved under its own name, so reconnecting just works.
:::

## Troubleshooting

There are two errors you're likely to run into when getting started.

**Connection errors.** If you see an `APIConnectionError` (or a "connection refused" message), raghilda couldn't reach Ollama at the configured `base_url`. Check that the Ollama app is running, or start the server yourself with `ollama serve`. If Ollama is on another machine, double-check the address and port.

**Model not found.** An error like `model 'embeddinggemma-2:latest' not found` means Ollama is running but the model hasn't been pulled. Run `ollama pull embeddinggemma-2` (or whichever model you've configured) and try again.

Both errors appear as soon as raghilda first contacts Ollama, which is usually at `DuckDBStore.create()`, so a quick test store is an easy way to confirm your setup before starting a large ingest. If you run into something else, Ollama's [troubleshooting guide](https://docs.ollama.com/troubleshooting) explains where to find the server logs, which usually say what went wrong.

## Parameters

`EmbeddingOllama` takes four parameters. All of them are optional, so a standard local install of Ollama needs no arguments at all:

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | `"embeddinggemma-2:latest"` | Ollama embedding model name, as shown by `ollama list` |
| `base_url` | `"http://localhost:11434/v1"` | Address of Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API |
| `api_key` | `None` | Only needed behind an authenticating proxy. A placeholder is used if `None` |
| `batch_size` | `20` | Texts per API call |

In practice, the parameters you're most likely to change are `model` and, if Ollama runs somewhere other than your own machine, `base_url`. All of them except `api_key` are saved with the store, so a reconnected store uses the same model and server. For the full API details, see the [`EmbeddingOllama` reference page](/reference/embedding.EmbeddingOllama.qmd).

## Complete example

This example builds a store from two web pages and searches it. Apart from fetching the pages, everything runs on your own machine:

```{python}
#| eval: false
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingOllama
from raghilda.read import read_as_markdown
from raghilda.chunker import MarkdownChunker

store = DuckDBStore.create(
    location="docs.db",
    embed=EmbeddingOllama(model="embeddinggemma-2:latest"),
    name="docs",
    title="My Documentation",
    overwrite=True,
)

chunker = MarkdownChunker()
for url in ["https://example.com/doc1", "https://example.com/doc2"]:
    store.upsert(chunker.chunk(read_as_markdown(url)))

store.build_index()

chunks = store.retrieve("How do I configure authentication?", top_k=5)
for chunk in chunks:
    print(chunk.text[:200])
```

If you'd also like the chat side of your RAG application to run locally, [chatlas](chatlas-integration.qmd) can talk to Ollama through `ChatOllama`, so the whole pipeline (from embedding to answer generation) stays on your machine.

## Using Ollama with ChromaDB

When you pass `EmbeddingOllama` to `ChromaDBStore`, raghilda wraps it in an adapter so that ChromaDB can call it. The provider is restored automatically when you reconnect from Python, but ChromaDB clients in other languages won't be able to use the collection's embedding function. See [ChromaDB Embedding Functions](chromadb-embedding-functions.qmd) for details.

## When to use Ollama

`EmbeddingOllama` is a good fit when:

- your content shouldn't be sent to a third-party API
- you're already using Ollama for local chat models
- you want local embeddings without installing PyTorch into your Python environment
- you'd like one embedding server shared by several projects or machines

Ollama and [SentenceTransformers](embedding-sentence-transformers.qmd) both keep embeddings local, and they differ mainly in where the model runs. SentenceTransformers loads the model inside your Python process and gives you access to anything on Hugging Face. Ollama runs models in a separate server, which keeps your Python environment light and lets other tools share the same models.
